findings.text: §28 declares `implementable` but its deliverable is already landed at the reviewed base: `afb14d67a8 land(a-moved-head-still-gets-a-review)` and `ecb87b0893 fix(crew): compose a review when a moved head cannot carry` are ancestors of the base `ffe72af6753f`, `ecb87b0893` adds `tests/test_a_moved_head_still_gets_a_review.py` (the exact write path §28 names) whose 5 cases pass here in 2.34 s, and primary carries `57fd763160 promote(r-20261118T105428794719-a-moved-head-still-gets-a-review): passed` — so a node dispatched on this text would re-implement landed work

findings.reason: a control that cannot fail leaves the node's gate resting on a suite that already passes, so the section cannot show its guard fires.
findings.text: §28's negative control, "at the base revision the request raises with a message naming the two heads", cannot fire: `carry_review_forward` checks the brief before storing and returns `{"carried": False, "reason": brief_refusal}` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2067-2075), the request path then composes a light review of the delta (same file, :3276-3283) instead of raising, and the only raise is `store_review`'s own refusal for a re-filed record (reckon/crew/review.py:3680-3682); measured, the named test file passes 5/5 at this base

findings.reason: a repair pointed at the carry-and-store raise would find nothing to fix, and the real failure the observation records would go unaddressed.
findings.text: §28's Why attributes the failure to the carry path raising "because the record describes the new head while its brief names the old one", but at the same base that path refuses cleanly and returns the reason rather than raising, and `review_module.store_review(carried)` is reached only after the brief check passes (:2079); the section's evidence (a run review-missing for 145 minutes with a sweep-failed row) is therefore not explained by the mechanism it names
